name: Gutti Vankaya Kura
subtitle: small brinjals slit and stuffed with a peanut, sesame and tamarind masala

ingredients.qty: 10 small purple brinjals, about 500g, stalks left on

ingredients.note: guntur chilli powder for a proper Andhra heat

ingredients.qty: a walnut-sized ball, soaked in 150ml hot water

prepNotes: Choose small, firm, glossy brinjals with green stalks. Big ones cannot be stuffed and go seedy.
Slit the brinjals into quarters from the base but leave the stalk end joined, and drop them into salted water until you stuff them so they do not brown.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes and strain.

steps.text: Dry roast the peanuts for 4 minutes until the skins blister, then the sesame for 1 minute until it pops, then the dried coconut for 1 minute. Cool.
steps.tip: Roast each one separately. They brown at completely different speeds.

steps.text: Rub the peanut skins off, then grind the peanuts, sesame and coconut with the garlic, ginger, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder, turmeric and salt to a coarse dry masala.
Loosen the masala with 3 tbsp of the tamarind water to a thick stuffing paste.
Drain the brinjals, pat dry and pack the paste into each slit, keeping any leftover masala aside.
steps.tip: Do not overstuff. A crammed brinjal splits open in the pan and the masala scatters.

steps.text: Heat the groundnut oil in a wide kadhai and crackle the mustard and cumin seeds with the curry leaves.
Add the chopped onion and fry 6 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Lay the stuffed brinjals in a single layer, cover and cook 8 minutes over low heat, turning them gently twice.
steps.tip: Turn them with tongs by the stalk. A spoon will break them apart.

steps.text: Stir the remaining masala into the rest of the tamarind water with the jaggery and pour it around the brinjals.
Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes over low heat until the brinjals are collapsing-soft and the gravy is thick and the oil rises to the surface.
steps.tip: The oil separating out is the sign it is done; the masala tastes raw before that.

steps.text: Scatter the coriander and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice or jonna rotte.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently in a pan with 2 tbsp water; do not stir hard or the brinjals disintegrate.
